text:
At closing, a rushed handover led the care lead to ask questions about a pet travel case that had not been fully settled. Incident report: late handover at the Companion Animal Travel Desk. The outgoing team member passed along notes in a hurry, and the incoming care lead had to rebuild the full picture from scattered details. The traveler and pet were still being supported, but the record had a gap where the next action should have been clear. The senior coordinator stepped in, reviewed the file, and confirmed the current status before any further contact was made. The passenger coordinator then spoke with the traveler, explained the required steps in plain language, and checked that the crate, documents, and animal care notes were all aligned. <<FACT F118>> The team kept the tone calm and practical so the traveler would not feel brushed aside.

A separate delay concern was also raised during the same review. <<FACT F109>> The senior coordinator documented the issue, confirmed the handoff problem, and asked for a cleaner end-of-shift summary next time.

After the immediate review, the desk updated the case notes, flagged the missing handover detail, and set the file for follow-up by the morning team. The staff member involved was reminded to pause, verify each step, and leave a complete record before closing the desk. This was handled as a service recovery matter, and the follow-up will focus on clearer handover habits.
